## Costco (COST) — revenue projection, next two quarters

**These are projections from a deterministic model, not filed figures.**

### Primary: seasonal trend model (20 quarters of history)

| Fiscal quarter ending | Projected revenue | 95% range |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-02 (FQ4'26) | **$87.16B** | $82.66B – $91.67B |
| 2026-10-25 (FQ1'27) | **$69.66B** | $65.10B – $74.23B |

**Assumptions the model fitted (must travel with the numbers):**
- Method: linear trend + fiscal-quarter seasonal adjustment; 20 historical quarters used.
- Slope: **+$937.7M per quarter**; intercept $54.54B.
- Fit quality: **R² = 0.30 before seasonal adjustment** — this just clears the tool's 0.30 minimum, so the underlying trend is weak and the projection leans heavily on the seasonal factors.
- Seasonal factors by fiscal-quarter position: Q1 **+$13.87B**, Q2 **−$4.57B**, Q3 **−$4.13B**, Q4 **−$5.16B**. (The large "Q1" factor reflects Costco's 16/17-week fourth quarter versus 12-week quarters elsewhere — the position labels in the model don't map to Costco's fiscal-quarter names, but the big positive factor is picking up the long quarter, which is why the August period projects near $87B.)
- Interval is a 95% normal approximation off deseasonalized in-sample residuals, not a formal prediction interval.

### Why not the other methods
- **Trend (12 quarters): refused.** Reason given: "linear trend fit quality is too low to project from (R²=0.05 < 0.3)."
- **Seasonal on 12 quarters: refused**, same reason (R²=0.05). Only extending to 20 quarters produced an acceptable fit.
- **Growth (compounding average QoQ growth, 12 quarters): available but far less usable** — $71.14B for the quarter ending 2026-08-02 and $71.75B for 2026-10-25, on an average QoQ growth rate of just **0.87%** with a growth-rate standard deviation of **20.8%**. That volatility is Costco's quarter-length seasonality, not real business volatility, and it blows the interval out to $25.5B–$141.4B by the second period. I'd treat the seasonal model as the more meaningful of the two.

### Filed history the model is fitted on (for context)
Most recent actuals, all from SEC filings: FQ3'26 ending 2026-05-10 **$70.53B** (filed 2026-06-03), FQ2'26 ending 2026-02-15 **$69.60B** (filed 2026-03-11), FQ1'26 ending 2025-11-23 **$67.31B** (filed 2025-12-17). Note that the long fourth quarters in the history — e.g. **$86.16B** for the period ending 2025-08-31 and **$79.70B** for 2024-09-01 — are **derived** figures (FY total minus Q1–Q3), not directly filed quarterly facts, so the seasonal factor for that position rests partly on synthesized data.

Also worth flagging: Costco does not report gross profit in its XBRL filings, so no margin-based cross-check is possible here.
